newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Pacific Cement seeks SEC nod on share offer.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Cement seeks SEC nod on share offer.

text.p: Pacific Cement Corp sought on Monday approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission to undertake a public offering of shares.
Documents submitted by the firm to the SEC showed the company proposes to sell 115.5 million shares at a price ranging from three to five pesos.
Proceeds of the offer will be used to finance capital expenditures and repay bridge financing taken for the company's upgrading program.

The company started a 350 million-peso programme in late 1995 that would raise its capacity to 370,000 tonnes from 220,000 tonnes per year and convert to the dry from the wet kiln process to reduce energy consumption.
Pacific posted a net income of 27.8 million pesos in 1995 from 15.9 million pesos in 1994. It projects a net income of 139.9 million pesos in 1996 before going down to 85 million pesos in 1997.
As of December 1995, the company accounted for 2.0 percent of total industry sales.
The company is owned 81 percent by Jose L. Cortes.

Pacific was listed in the Manila and Makati stock exchanges in 1969 but its shares had not been traded for the past 20 years. It expects trading to be reactivated with the registration and sale of these shares.
The public currently accounts for 0.2 percent of the outstanding shares of the company. After the offering, the public is expected to own 33.1 percent.
The proposed underwriter of the offer is RCBC Capital Corp.
